newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis receives cash from Sudan partners.
newsitem.headline: Arakis receives cash from Sudan partners.

text.p: Arakis Energy Corp has pocketed the first check from its partners in a series of cash calls that will fund development of the group's US$1 billion Sudan oil project, the company said on Tuesday.
Arakis said 30-percent partner Petronas, Malaysia's state oil company, forwarded its portion of the consortium's December cash call early Tuesday.
China National Petroleum Corp, the project's 40-percent participant, has also advised Arakis in writing that its portion of the funds would be forwarded within three days, Arakis said.
Investors have been waiting for Arakis to receive money from its partners as proof of the project's credibility.
Arakis in early December announced a long-awaited joint venture deal to develop the 12.2 million acre oil concession and build a 950-mile pipeline to the Red Sea from Southern Sudan.
Partners include Arakis with 25 percent, CNPC with 40 percent, Petronas with 30 percent and the government of Sudan with five percent.
Under the deal, the partners will form a joint operating company to oversee development of the project, which is slated to start production of 150,000 barrels of oil per day by 1999.

The interim agreement allowed Arakis to be credited for US$140 million it spent on the acreage until November 29, as well as a possible US$60 million more for "appraised value-added," or improvements made to the properties.

The financial credit in the agreement translates into no project expenditures from Arakis's own coffers for "a significant period of time" while the partners match Arakis's previous spending, the company said.
Arakis said it had prepared an earlier December cash call based on its expectations of project spending as operator.

However, after meetings in Calgary between Arakis and its partners starting in the third week of December, some of the plans were deferred until 1997 and the cash call was revised, the company said. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
